decisions.mark: states that staleness is THREE distinguishable axes rather than one flag, and names them
explains that each axis is cleared by a DIFFERENT action — a rebuild for data, a client restart for code — which is why one flag would not have been enough
identifies that the schema axis can be UNRESOLVABLE — when the index is newer than the server, no rebuild clears it, because rebuilding re-stamps the same newer version
states the read/write asymmetry on the code axis: READS stay current because query tools open the database per call, while a BUILD through a stale process writes old pipeline logic
identifies that the write path REFUSES rather than warning, and that the refusal is placed ahead of the build decision so a force flag cannot override it
states that the annotation RIDES ON EVERY QUERY REPLY rather than waiting to be asked for, and that it is empty on a current tool
identifies that measuring staleness NEVER raises — a failed measurement degrades to no annotation rather than turning a successful reply into an error
states that a routed reply is annotated for the repository it actually read, not for the server's default target
identifies that the annotation is fitted to the response budget by degrading its wording rather than by dropping the warning
